program_name: Bachelor in Social Education (IT: Laurea in Scienze dell'Educazione; DE: Bachelor in Sozialpädagogik / Bachelorstudium Sozialpädagogik). Note the Italian name is 'Scienze dell'Educazione', NOT 'Educazione Sociale' — the official Italian programme page and both signed 2026/27 ranking-list decrees use 'Scienze dell'Educazione (L-19)' and 'Sozialpädagogik (L-19)'. Faculty of Education (Facoltà di Scienze della Formazione).
teaching_language: Trilingual (Italian / German / English). The 'At a glance' box states: 'Courses will be taught in: Italian, German and English (trilingual)' — note Italian is listed FIRST here, unlike the Bolzano programmes. English is the SMALLEST of the three languages, not the main one. Per-module language tags from the official course-offering pages (2026/27, cohort 'enrolled from 2025') give: YEAR 1 (61 CP) — German 17 CP (Foundations of General Education 4; Qualitative Research Methods 7; Child and Adolescent Psychiatry 4; LAB Reflection on Social Pedagogical Practice 2), Italian 18 CP (Foundations of Social Education 4; LAB Pedagogy of Play and Narration 2; Foundations of General Sociology 5; Quantitative Research Methods 7), English only 8 CP (Anthropological Research for Socio-Educational Interventions 4; Introduction to Methods and Fields of Social Education 4), plus one 10 CP module tagged IT+DE (Foundations of Psychology for Educational Work) and 8 CP language-neutral (free choice 4, internship 4). YEAR 2 (60 CP) — German 14 CP (Lifelong Learning 9; Intercultural Education and Intersectionality 5), one 9 CP module tagged EN+DE (Inclusion, Marginality and Socio-Educational Practice), 27 CP tagged IT+EN (Sustainability and Global Citizenship 10; Social Policy and Services 8; Physical Activity, Health and Wellbeing 9), and 10 CP internship. YEAR 3 (59 CP) — per-module languages not yet published for the 2026/27 offering (the 2025 cohort only reaches year 3 in 2027/28); the only certain English element is 'English for Professional Purposes' 3 CP, alongside 21 CP language-neutral (free choice 8, internship 10, final exam 3). CONCLUSION: German and Italian each carry roughly twice the English-only credit load in year 1, both are compulsory from the FIRST semester, and there is no English-only pathway at any point. [uncertain] — the credit split is reconstructed from per-module language tags on the course-offering pages combined with the brochure study plan; the two sub-courses of 'Foundations of Psychology for Educational Work' (10 CP, tagged IT+DE) could not be resolved individually, and year-3 tags are unpublished.
campus: Brixen-Bressanone (Faculty of Education campus, Regensburger Allee 16 / viale Ratisbona 16, 39042 Brixen-Bressanone; Faculty Secretariat at Kreuzgasse 7 / via della Croce 7). The 'At a glance' box states simply 'Campus: Brixen-Bressanone'. This is unibz's second-largest campus, about 40 km north of Bolzano, and is German-Italian in character rather than English-facing. Not Bozen-Bolzano, not NOI Techpark, not Bruneck-Brunico, not Trento, not Innsbruck. IMPORTANT: the compulsory admission interview is also held physically in Brixen-Bressanone, so the campus location is part of the admission burden, not only of the study experience.
degree_class: L-19 (Scienze dell'educazione e della formazione / Education and Training Sciences). 180 ECTS, 3 years, 61 CP in year 1, 60 CP in year 2, 59 CP in year 3. The degree gives access to the regulated profession of socio-pedagogical educator (educatore professionale socio-pedagogico) under Italian law.
offered_in_2026_27: Yes — actively offered, actively recruiting, and TIME-CRITICAL AT THE VERIFICATION DATE. The Early Bird and Late ranking lists for 2026/27 have both been published (25 + 9 EU admitted). Crucially, unibz's additional-application-session page lists 'Bachelor in Social Education' under the Faculty of Education among the programmes accepting applications from 18/08/2026 to 04/09/2026 (EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only), with studies starting October 2026. Verified 2026-08-29: that window closes at noon on 04/09/2026, i.e. six days later, with the admission interview already scheduled for 11/09/2026.
is_new_programme: No — established programme, but with a study-plan reform effective 2025/26. The programme page maintains two separate curricula: 'Course Offering — Enrolled from 2025' (current) and 'Course Offering — enrolled before 2025' (legacy), which is the standard unibz marker of a restructured, not a new, degree. Social pedagogy (Sozialpädagogik) has been a core offering of the Brixen-Bressanone Faculty of Education since the faculty's foundation, and a 2025/26 brochure for this programme exists at the same asset path (?v=98). 2026/27 is therefore at least the second intake under the reformed 2025 study plan, and the programme itself is long-standing. The Faculty of Education ranked first in the 2025 Censis ranking in the education-sciences sector.
majors_tracks_study_plans: NO majors, NO tracks, NO study-plan variants and no dual-study four-year variant. All students follow a single common curriculum of 180 CP over three years. The only points of individual choice are the free-choice credits (4 CP in year 1 + 8 CP in year 3 = 12 CP total, selectable from a broad elective catalogue that includes Digital Humanities 3 CP EN, Gender and Sexuality Studies 4 CP EN, Public Speaking 2 CP DE/IT, Systemic Social Work 4 CP DE, Motivational Interviewing in Social Work 4 CP IT, Photography 3 CP DE, Solidarity Economy and Social Agriculture 4 CP DE and roughly 30 further options), the choice of internship placement, and the thesis topic. Structure: core subjects are psychology, sociology, pedagogy and anthropology, delivered as large integrated modules each combining lecture courses with compulsory LAB workshops. Two supervised professional internships of 200 hours each run in the 2nd and 3rd year (4 CP orientation placement in year 1, 10 CP in year 2, 10 CP in year 3). Part-time enrolment is available as a general unibz option, chosen after initial enrolment in October. Attendance rules are unusually strict: workshop attendance is compulsory, justified absences must be compensated with extra activities, and internship hours must be completed in full.
english_only_accessibility: effectively-closed for a candidate who knows only English. This is one of the HARDEST unibz trilingual programmes for an international applicant, on three independent grounds. (1) ENTRY LANGUAGE GATE: B2 is required in the 1st language AND B2 in the 2nd language, and failure means exclusion from the admission procedure rather than a lower rank ('otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure'). A candidate certifying only English satisfies one language and is excluded outright. The concrete minimum for a Turkish applicant is English B2 + German B2 or Italian B2 — a full CEFR step harder than the B2/B1 demanded by, for example, the Bachelor in Food and Enogastronomy Sciences. The admission PDF confirms the consequence for exam booking: 'Please note that you can only register for B2 level exams.' (2) COMPULSORY IN-PERSON INTERVIEW IN BRIXEN carrying 80 of the 100 available points, held in English, German or Italian; video conference is granted only on a written and motivated request for 'serious logistical difficulties' filed at least 7 days ahead, so a candidate abroad depends on a discretionary concession for the single most heavily weighted element of the selection. (3) CURRICULUM: English is the smallest teaching language — only 8 CP of year 1 is English-only against 17 CP German and 18 CP Italian — German and Italian are both compulsory from the first semester, and graduation demands C1/C1/B2 across all three languages, the full-strength trilingual exit profile. EMPIRICAL SIGNAL: no non-EU applicant living abroad appears as admitted in the 2026/27 Early Bird decree at all (see places_quotas), against a reserved quota of 4, while all 25 EU places filled — consistent with the language and interview gates being decisive for international candidates.
admission_type: Restricted access (numero programmato / limited places) with a merit-based ranking list, selected by INTERVIEW plus documentary assessment. There is NO entrance exam, no TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT and no portfolio. The instruments are: an eliminatory language-eligibility gate (B2 in the 1st language + B2 in the 2nd), a cover/motivation letter of maximum 6,000 characters, a compulsory admission interview worth up to 80 points, and an assessment of prior social-work experience worth up to 20 points. Separate ranking lists are drawn up for (a) EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment and (b) non-EU citizens living abroad. This is one of only a handful of unibz bachelor programmes where a live interview — not school grades — is the dominant selection instrument; school-leaving grades carry NO points in this rubric at all.
academic_requirements: Required qualification (one of): (a) a secondary school leaving certificate of the Italian system; or (b) an equivalent qualification obtained abroad. A foreign school-leaving certificate counts as equivalent only if obtained after 12 years of education AND the applicant attended at least the last two years in that foreign school system (stated example: an Irish Leaving Certificate obtained after only one year is not sufficient). The Italian Ministry of Education, University and Research sets additional specific requirements for holders of certain certificates — American high school diplomas and British and Greek certificates are named explicitly; those applicants should contact apply@unibz.it (Advisory Service). Language requirements (1st language B2, 2nd language B2) are a separate and eliminatory condition. NOTABLE: unlike the science-facing unibz bachelors, this programme states NO subject-specific preparation requirement (no mathematics, physics, chemistry or biology prerequisite) and consequently assigns no OFA — see ofa_rules. No ECTS/SSD credit requirements apply, those being master-level instruments. National rule: simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 study programmes is allowed provided they do not belong to the same class (e.g. not L-18/L-18) and differ in at least 2/3 of course contents.
entry_exam_or_test: NONE. No unibz admission exam, no TOLC-I, no CENT-S, no SAT, no subject test and no written test of any kind. The selection instrument is an oral admission interview (see 'interview'), not an examination. The only examinations connected with admission are LANGUAGE exams at the unibz Language Centre, and only for applicants who choose that route of proof: Early Bird — 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late — 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026). These are held ONLINE. Because this programme requires B2/B2, 'you can only register for B2 level exams' — B1 exams cannot be booked, unlike programmes with a B1 second-language threshold. No language-exam session is listed for the Additional Application Session, so applicants in that window must already hold recognised proof. Separately, AFTER admission there is a non-selective third-language placement test for admitted students who cannot certify their third language, with details communicated by e-mail.
selection_scoring: Three criteria, maximum 100 points, awarded by the Faculty Admission Committee: (1) COVER LETTER, maximum 6,000 characters, indicating prior knowledge — no point value is stated for the letter itself; (2) ADMISSION INTERVIEW, MAX. 80 POINTS, assessing 'knowledge and understanding of current social issues and communication skills'; (3) EXPERIENCE IN THE FIELD OF SOCIAL WORK, MAX. 20 POINTS. Tie-break: priority to the YOUNGEST candidate. Critical structural features: school-leaving grades carry ZERO weight (unlike almost every other unibz bachelor, which scores grade averages), so the interview alone determines 80% of the score; and the Admission Committee 'will only evaluate the documents uploaded in the portal by the application deadline'. NO minimum passing threshold is published for this programme — unlike Design (42/100), Critical Creative Practices (60/100), EMMA (55/95) or Entrepreneurship (70/100). COMPETITION SIGNAL: unlike most unibz ranking lists, the 2026/27 decrees for this programme publish only ranking positions and Applicant IDs, with NO scores at all, so no score distribution or de facto cut-off can be derived. The Early Bird list filled all 25 EU places exactly and the Late list admitted 9 of 10, so the programme is close to fully subscribed — materially more competitive than the undersubscribed Bolzano science bachelors. [uncertain] — whether the cover letter carries its own points (making the stated 80+20 an incomplete rubric) or serves as an unscored input to the interview is not stated in any published source.
bonus_points: NONE. The rubric is closed at 80 interview points + 20 social-work-experience points. There is no Webometrics university-ranking bonus (that applies to Master in Software Engineering and Master in Computing for Data Science), no GMAT/GRE bonus (Accounting and Finance), no start-up project bonus (Entrepreneurship), no extracurricular bonus of the Computer Science type and no school-grade component. The only preference mechanism in the entire procedure is the age tie-break in favour of the younger candidate. The nearest thing to a 'bonus' is the 20-point social-work-experience component, which is a scored criterion rather than a bonus and is the only place where a candidate can bank points before the interview day — worth treating as the decisive differentiator for applicants who cannot rely on native-level German or Italian in the interview.
portfolio_and_materials: One substantive written submission only: a COVER LETTER (also called presentation/motivation letter) of MAXIMUM 6,000 CHARACTERS, indicating the applicant's prior knowledge. The admission PDF is explicit that in the application portal 'you shall: upload the cover letter'. No portfolio, no video, no project proposal, no reference letters, no CV and no writing sample are required, and no file-size or page limits are published because no other materials exist. There is no 'study career' Excel template — that is a master-level requirement. Documentation of prior social-work experience must be uploaded for the 20-point experience criterion; the admission document does not specify an accepted format or evidence standard for it. All documents must be in the portal by the application deadline, since the Admission Committee evaluates only what was uploaded by then; once submitted the application cannot be modified, and forms filled in but not correctly sent are disregarded. Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list. [uncertain] — the required evidence format for the social-work-experience criterion (certificates, employer letters, self-declaration) is not published.
interview: YES — compulsory, in person, and the dominant selection instrument (max. 80 of 100 points). Purpose: 'to assess knowledge and understanding of current social issues and communication skills'. LOCATION: Brixen-Bressanone; the precise location and time are published on www.unibz.it. LANGUAGE OF CHOICE: the candidate may choose to hold the admission colloquium in ENGLISH, GERMAN OR ITALIAN — the single most important accessibility concession in this programme, since an English-speaking candidate who has certified B2 German or Italian may still be interviewed in English. REMOTE OPTION: 'If you are unable to attend the interview appointment due to serious logistical difficulties, it is possible to hold the interview in a video conference. You must provide a written and motivated request to the Faculty Secretariat at least 7 days before the date of the interview' — discretionary, not a right, and a hard 7-day lead time. PUBLISHED 2026/27 INTERVIEW DATES: Early Bird 19/05/2026; Late Application 21/07/2026; Additional Application Session 11/09/2026. Each date sits between its application deadline and its ranking-list publication date, so it is a fixed, unavoidable calendar commitment. Contact for the video-conference request: Faculty of Education Secretariat, faculty.education@unibz.it, +39 0472 014000, Kreuzgasse 7, 39042 Brixen-Bressanone.
conditional_admission: Applicants still in their final year of upper secondary school may apply — the diploma is uploaded at enrolment: 'if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment'. This is the normal case rather than a special regime, and is workable here precisely because school grades carry no points in the rubric. Holders of a foreign qualification are admitted with reserve: unibz performs its own checks and 'reserves the right to request additional documents', and an applicant who turns out not to possess a valid admission qualification 'can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment'. Non-EU applicants living abroad are additionally admitted with reserve pending the Italian consulate's confirmation. Refund rule tied to this: fees paid to secure a place are non-refundable EXCEPT if the applicant fails the secondary-school final exam (maturità) or, for non-EU applicants living abroad, does not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities. [uncertain] — the ≥120/140 ECTS conditional-admission thresholds and the 11/12/2026 late-enrolment window in the field schema are MASTER-level rules and do not apply to this bachelor programme; no bachelor equivalent is published.
ofa_rules: NO OFA. This programme assigns no additional learning obligations (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi) — the 2026/27 admission-information document contains no OFA section, no minimum grade-average threshold and no catch-up or pre-course requirement, and no mathematics pre-course is scheduled. This is a genuine structural difference from the unibz programmes that do use OFA: the economics programmes (Economics and Management, Economics Politics and Ethics, Tourism Sport and Event Management) assign test-based OFA after a compulsory mathematics test, and Food and Enogastronomy Sciences and Computer Science assign grade-based OFA. Here no quantitative school preparation is assessed at all, because school grades are not scored. The functional equivalent of a remedial obligation in this programme is purely linguistic: an admitted student who cannot certify the third language must sit a placement test and follow an assigned learning path, and from the 2nd semester of the first year a B1 level in the third language is required in order to take curricular examinations held in that language.
language_requirements: The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English, and the rule is eliminatory: 'The official teaching languages are German, Italian and English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure'. ENTRY (to gain admission): 1st language B2, 2nd language B2, 3rd language no level required. FROM THE 2ND SEMESTER OF THE FIRST YEAR: B1 in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations in that language. EXIT (to graduate): 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B2 — the standard full-strength unibz trilingual exit profile. Language positions are defined by the applicant's own proficiency, not by which language it is: 'Your first language is the language in which you have the highest level of proficiency (B2 or C1). Your third language is instead the language in which you are weaker (or in which you are an absolute beginner).' Certification is MANDATORY for the 1st and 2nd language and recommended (from B1 upwards) for the 3rd. Because B2/B2 is required, only B2-level Language Centre exams can be booked. Admitted students who cannot certify the third language take a placement test and are assigned a learning path aiming at B2 'as soon as possible'. Language Centre courses are free: extensive courses 4 h/week during semesters, intensive courses 8 h/week between semesters, and a three-week pre-semester intensive session 01-18/09/2026 (Mon-Fri, 6 h/day). A1 beginner courses are offered ONLY in that September pre-semester session and no longer during the academic year, so absolute beginners must start there. Target levels in the third language: B1 by the end of year 1, B2 by the end of year 2. Practical weight for this programme: the curriculum makes the third language unavoidable — German carries 17 CP and Italian 18 CP of English-free teaching already in year 1 — so the B1-from-semester-2 rule genuinely blocks exams rather than being a formality.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language: B2 — 2nd language: B2 — 3rd language: no level required (B1 needed from the 2nd semester of year 1 to sit exams in that language). This 'B2/B2/none' pattern is the standard-strength unibz trilingual entry profile: identical to the Bachelor in Computer Science, one step HARDER than Food and Enogastronomy Sciences (B2/B1/none) and one step easier than Public Policy and Accounting and Finance (C1/B2/none). Position is set by the candidate's own strength ranking, not by which language it is, so a Turkish applicant with strong English typically registers English as the 1st language and must then certify B2 in German or Italian as the 2nd. Direct booking consequence stated in the admission document: 'Please note that you can only register for B2 level exams' — B1 Language Centre exams are not bookable for this programme, so there is no partial-credit route and no 'admission at B1 if places remain' clause of the kind that appears in the Food and Enogastronomy ranking decrees.
exit_levels: To graduate: 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B2 (CEFR). This is the full-strength unibz trilingual exit profile — one step harder in the second language than Food and Enogastronomy Sciences (C1/B2/B2). A student admitted at B2/B2/none must therefore raise BOTH the first and second languages to C1 and go from zero to B2 in the third language within three years, i.e. reach professional working proficiency in three languages to obtain the degree. Free Language Centre courses are structured to support this (third language: B1 by end of year 1, B2 by end of year 2). This exit requirement, not the entry gate, is the single largest long-run risk for an international student in this programme and should be treated as a genuine graduation condition rather than an administrative formality.
third_language_exam_threshold: B1 in the third language is the minimum requirement for taking curricular examinations held in that language, applying from the 2ND SEMESTER OF THE FIRST YEAR. The admission document states this as its own dated rule rather than as general guidance. The constraint bites harder here than in most unibz programmes because the first year is not English-led: German-tagged modules carry 17 CP and Italian-tagged modules 18 CP in year 1 alone, against only 8 CP of English-only teaching, plus a 10 CP module tagged IT+DE. A student whose third language is German or Italian therefore risks being blocked from a large share of first- and second-year examinations from semester 2 onward. There is no programme-specific mid-January English deadline of the kind applied to the Bachelor in Computer Science.
proof_pathways: Four recognised pathways. (1) The main teaching language of the final high-school year, if German, Italian or English — recognised as C1 (Ladin upper secondary schools: recognised as B2 in German and Italian); for foreign qualifications, if the medium of instruction is not clearly stated on the diploma, a letter or document issued by the high school stating it must also be uploaded. (2) A bachelor or master degree taught in Italian, German or English — recognised as C1; unibz graduates upload certificates obtained and/or declare Language Centre exams passed (B2, B2+ or C1); foreign degrees need a university letter stating the medium of instruction if not on the degree. (3) A recognised language certificate from the official unibz list; if it cannot be uploaded it may be sent by e-mail as a PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline. (4) Language exams organised by the unibz Language Centre, held ONLINE, registered through the application portal under 'enrol for language exams' after creating an application — Early Bird: 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026); Late: 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026); B2 level only for this programme. If an application is started outside a registration period, the applicant must return to the portal during one of the listed periods. Additional route for foreign and bi-/multilingual schools: if CEFR levels for German, Italian or English are explicitly stated on the graduation diploma and all four skills (reading, listening, speaking, writing) were assessed, those levels are accepted as proof for the 2nd and/or 3rd language, subject to Language Centre approval. Administrative detail: a final certificate awarded by an Italian public institution requires a self-declaration; one awarded by a foreign public institution requires an uploaded scanned copy of the original. PLANNING WARNING: no Language Centre exam session is published for the Additional Application Session (18/08-04/09/2026), so applicants in that window must already hold recognised proof of B2/B2.
certificate_rules: Governed by Resolution of the University Council no. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas — Students and applicants'; DE: Beschluss des Universitätsrates Nr. 16/2026; IT: Delibera del Consiglio dell'Università n. 16/2026). Rules: (1) the certificate must include the assessment of ALL FOUR SKILLS and be issued by the certification organisation itself; (2) it must show adequate performance in all skills as an overall grade, or the detailed assessment must appear on the certificate or in appropriate documentation from the issuer; (3) if no overall result and/or level is stated, THE LOWEST LEVEL REACHED IN ANY SUB-SKILL is decisive for determining the level, provided that part was passed; (4) there is NO COMPENSATION for failed parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless the certification organisation itself provides them; (5) certificates obtained by taking an online 'home edition' exam are NOT recognised, except those explicitly indicated in the list (a handful are flagged '* Also accepted as home edition'); (6) certificates covering single skills issued by different organisations are not accepted; (7) certificates of participation, end-of-course tests and placement-test results are not recognised; (8) certificates issued by individual lecturers, lettori or language teachers are not recognised; (9) DAAD certificates are NOT recognised — a significant trap for applicants planning to certify German cheaply. VALIDITY: international language certificates must not be older than FIVE YEARS at the date of submission, with the entire calendar year counting from 1 January (certificates issued from 1 January of the fifth preceding year remain valid). Items listed under 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' have unlimited validity. Full list: https://www.unibz.it/assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf
application_deadline_eu: Three sessions for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (unibz publishes DD/MM/YYYY; ISO normalised below). All deadlines are 'by noon local time'. EARLY BIRD APPLICATION: 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. LATE APPLICATION (EU only): 28/05/2026 - 08/07/2026 = 2026-05-28 to 2026-07-08. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU only, opened by the Faculty in August/September if places remain — and it WAS opened for this programme in 2026/27): 18/08/2026 - 04/09/2026 = 2026-08-18 to 2026-09-04. EU applicants may apply for more than one study programme, and an applicant excluded in one session may apply again in the next. VERIFIED 2026-08-29: the Additional Application Session is the only window currently open and closes at noon on 2026-09-04, with the admission interview on 2026-09-11 — so an applicant entering now has about six days to apply and must already hold B2/B2 language proof, since no Language Centre exam session is scheduled for this window.
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE window only for non-EU citizens living outside Italy: the EARLY BIRD APPLICATION, 02/03/2026 - 28/04/2026 by noon local time = 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28. 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' Non-EU applicants living abroad are NOT eligible for the Late Application or the Additional Application Session, pay a non-refundable €50 application fee, are ranked on a separate list against a separate 4-place quota, and must additionally pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (one programme only) for the study visa. They must also attend the 19/05/2026 admission interview in Brixen-Bressanone, or obtain discretionary approval for a video conference at least 7 days beforehand — a substantial practical obstacle for a candidate still abroad and without a visa. For academic year 2026/27 this window is CLOSED; the next opportunity for a non-EU applicant living abroad is the 2027/28 Early Bird session, expected around March-April 2027.
parity_of_treatment: Two categories are treated as EU applicants — the critical third category for Turkish applicants: (1) citizens of Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State; (2) non-EU citizens holding a valid Italian permit to stay ('permesso di soggiorno') under article 39 paragraph 5 of Legislative Decree no. 286 of 25/07/1998 — for WORK, FAMILY reasons, POLITICAL or HUMANITARIAN ASYLUM, or RELIGIOUS reasons. Such applicants apply directly to the University and must submit a copy of the valid permit; if it has expired, a renewal request must be attached. A permit to stay for STUDY reasons or a visa for tourism is NOT sufficient. Critical warning, quoted from the admission document: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' The consequence is losing access to the Late and Additional sessions, being moved from the 35-place EU quota to the 4-place non-EU list, and incurring the €50 fee. For this programme in 2026/27 the distinction is decisive at the verification date: the parity route leads to a session still open until 04/09/2026, whereas the non-EU-abroad route closed on 28/04/2026.
places_quotas: Three separate quotas for 2026/27, confirmed by the admission-information document. EU CITIZENS AND CITIZENS GIVEN PARITY OF TREATMENT: Early Bird Application 25 places, Late Application 10 places — summarised on the programme page and brochure as 'Places available: 35 EU + 4 non-EU'. NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD: Early Bird Application 4 places, and no non-EU quota in any later session. Carry-over rule (EU/equivalent only): 'any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application'. ACTUAL 2026/27 UPTAKE — materially more competitive than the Bolzano science bachelors: Early Bird admitted exactly 25 EU/equivalent candidates, filling the EU Early Bird quota completely with no carry-over; Late admitted 9 against 10 places. Cumulative EU/equivalent admissions 34 against the 35-place EU quota, leaving a single place, which is consistent with the Faculty nonetheless opening the Additional Application Session. NON-EU OUTCOME: the signed Early Bird decree contains only an 'EU citizens and equivalent' ranking table and NO non-EU section at all, and the ranking-lists index publishes no separate non-EU list for this programme, indicating that no non-EU applicant living abroad was admitted against the 4 reserved places. [uncertain] — whether zero non-EU candidates applied, or applied and were excluded, cannot be determined because unlike other faculties the Education decrees publish neither scores nor exclusion lists.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: EARLY BIRD: admission interviews 19/05/2026; ranking lists published by 27/05/2026; payment of the 1st instalment of tuition fees (€600 — this is what secures the place) by 05/06/2026 noon; enrolment from 10/07/2026 to 06/08/2026 noon. LATE APPLICATION: admission interviews 21/07/2026; ranking lists by 30/07/2026; 1st instalment by 06/08/2026 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 06/08/2026 noon. ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION: admission interviews 11/09/2026; ranking lists by 18/09/2026; 1st instalment by 25/09/2026 noon; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 25/09/2026 noon. Missing either the payment or the enrolment deadline means automatic exclusion and the place passes to the next applicant on the list. An applicant admitted to more than one programme may secure up to 2 places by paying the instalment twice. Paying does NOT confer student status — only enrolment does — and there is no refund if you pay but do not enrol (exceptions: failing the maturità, or, for non-EU applicants abroad, not obtaining the documents from the Italian authorities). Enrolment is recommended as early as possible so that incomplete documents can still be uploaded before the deadline. Related deadline from the ranking decrees: applications for recognition of exams and additional activities from previous university studies must be completed online via the unibz Intranet by 18/09/2026. The signed decrees carry the standard 60-day right of appeal to the Administrative Court of Bolzano. required_documents: AT APPLICATION (online via https://aws.unibz.it/exup/): a valid ID card or passport, front and back — 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'; the completed online form; the COVER LETTER of maximum 6,000 characters, uploaded in the portal; documentation of any experience working in the field of social work (for the 20-point criterion); language certificates uploaded under 'upload language certificates' (mandatory for the 1st and 2nd language, recommended from B1 for the 3rd) and/or registration for Language Centre exams under 'enrol for language exams'; the diploma of the qualification if already obtained abroad (otherwise uploaded at enrolment); for non-EU citizens resident in Italy claiming parity of treatment, a copy of the valid permit to stay plus a renewal request if expired. NOTE: there is NO 'study career' Excel template for this programme (a master-level requirement) and NO school report cards or grade transcripts are required for scoring, since school grades carry no points. AT ENROLMENT, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must additionally upload: the secondary school diploma; an official translation of the diploma into Italian (not necessary for diplomas issued in German or English); and the ARDI and/or CIMEA statements described under credential_recognition. Once submitted the application cannot be modified, and forms filled in but not correctly sent are disregarded. Mendacious declarations are criminally prosecuted and cause automatic exclusion from the ranking list. Students transferring from another Italian university must give the Student Office a copy of the transfer application at the beginning of the academic year; non-EU students must hand in a copy of the residence permit once obtained, in person or by e-mail.
application_fee: €50, payable only by non-EU citizens living outside Italy. It is described as an administration fee and is explicitly NON-REFUNDABLE: 'Application fee: € 50. The fee is an administration fee and is non-refundable.' EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (including non-EU nationals holding a qualifying Italian permit to stay for work, family, asylum or religious reasons) pay no application fee. Since non-EU applicants living abroad have only the Early Bird window, the fee is payable once per admission cycle.
tuition_or_fees_link: Total tuition fees are €1,200 per year in two instalments: 1st instalment €600, including the €16 revenue stamp (marca da bollo) — this is the payment that secures the place after admission; 2nd instalment €600, due by March of the following year. Delayed payment of the second instalment results in a fine; unpaid fees make it impossible to take exams and block any transfer to another university or study programme. No refund if you drop out, interrupt your studies or are excluded. EXEMPTIONS: students with a disability recognised under article 3 paragraph 1 of Law No 104/1992, or with a disability up to or exceeding 66% (health-authority certificate to be handed in at the beginning of the academic year); and foreign students who have been granted a scholarship from the Italian government. Students awarded a scholarship by the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are entitled to a refund of the tuition fees. Fees information: https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/ and the programme's own admission-information PDF: https://www.unibz.it/assets/CoursesPDF/bachelor-in-social-education_admission-information_en_GB.pdf
scholarships_grants: NO programme-specific scholarship exists for this degree — unlike, for example, the Bachelor in Food and Enogastronomy Sciences with its €1,000 Meran-Merano awards. Only the general unibz and provincial routes apply. MAIN ROUTE: the income-based study grant from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano, applied for through the Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario / provincial e-government service, worth between €1,680 and €6,960 per year; recipients also receive a refund of their unibz tuition fees. MERIT ROUTE: students who, after the first year, achieve an average grade of 27/30 in their exams may apply for merit-based rather than income-based scholarships. CRITICAL RESTRICTION FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: 'Non-EU students can apply for a study grant only if they have a long-time residence permit or after they have had their residence in South Tyrol for at least one year without interruption' — a newly arrived non-EU first-year student is therefore effectively ineligible in year one, and because this programme has no programme-specific award, a Turkish first-year student should plan on NO scholarship income at all in year 1 and budget the full €800/month living cost plus €1,200 tuition. The South Tyrolean students association sh.asus assists with grant applications. Other listed sources: Italian government grants (which also confer tuition exemption), Austrian and German (BAföG) grants, DAAD summer-course scholarships, and loans from Italian banks. Contacts: study@unibz.it, +39 0471 012900. Reference: https://guide.unibz.it/en/life-on-campus/study-grants . credential_recognition: At enrolment, holders of a foreign secondary school qualification must upload the diploma plus an official translation into Italian (not necessary for diplomas issued in German or English), and then, depending on the education system: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, International Baccalaureate, European Baccalaureate — a Statement of Correspondence of the secondary school diploma, downloaded from ARDI (Automatic Recognition Database Italy, https://ardi.cimea.it/en); (b) non-EU countries that ARE signatories to the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Correspondence from ARDI AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA; (c) non-EU countries that are NOT signatories of the Lisbon Convention — a Statement of Comparability issued by CIMEA AND a Statement of Verification issued by CIMEA. Türkiye is a signatory of the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so Turkish applicants normally fall under case (b): ARDI Statement of Correspondence + CIMEA Statement of Verification. Both CIMEA documents are paid services with processing lead times, so they should be started well before the enrolment window rather than after admission. unibz performs its own checks on the foreign qualification and reserves the right to request additional documents in case of doubt; an applicant found not to possess a valid admission qualification can be excluded by Rector's decree even after enrolment. Note that, unlike grade-scored unibz programmes, this programme does NOT require the school's grading scale or pass mark to be supplied, because school grades are not part of the rubric. Signatory list: https://www.enic-naric.net/ ; CIMEA services: https://cimea-diplome.it/ . Recognition of credit points from previous university studies is possible only after enrolment, only where the exams taken elsewhere are equivalent in content to unibz courses, and — per the 2026/27 ranking decrees — must be requested online via the unibz Intranet by 18/09/2026.
non_eu_visa_process: Sequence for non-EU citizens living abroad: apply to unibz in the Early Bird window only (€50 non-refundable fee) → attend the admission interview on 19/05/2026 in Brixen-Bressanone, or obtain discretionary approval for a video conference by written motivated request at least 7 days earlier → appear on the separate non-EU ranking list (4 places) → if admitted, secure the place by paying the €600 first instalment by the published deadline → THEN pre-enrol on the Universitaly portal (https://www.universitaly.it/). The Universitaly application is MANDATORY, 'otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol', and only ONE study programme may be selected there. The Italian diplomatic authorities in the applicant's country then issue the study/university entry visa. unibz warns that applying does not guarantee an appointment at the Italian diplomatic-consular representation and that admission 'does not confer automatically any right to obtaining a visa'. FINANCIAL MEANS: at least €800 per month for living costs (accommodation, food, study materials, leisure, clothing) in the Bozen-Bolzano area, excluding tuition; total proof of at least €36,000 for a bachelor programme (€24,000 for a master); health insurance and visa expenses on top of that. AFTER ARRIVAL: the residence permit ('permesso di soggiorno') must be APPLIED FOR within 8 working days of arrival in Italy — contact the Advisory Service immediately on arrival — and once obtained a copy must be handed in at the Student Office in person or by e-mail. Student work is limited to no more than 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year. Refund exception: non-EU applicants abroad who pay the instalment but do not obtain the documents needed for enrolment from the Italian authorities are entitled to a refund. Programme-specific caution: the in-person interview requirement falls BEFORE any visa exists, making the video-conference concession effectively essential for a genuine overseas applicant. Reference: https://www.unibz.it/en/applicants/international/international-degree-seeking-applicants/degree-seeking-non-eu-citizens-living-abroad/

uncertainty_notes: Data year: all figures are for academic year 2026/27; the admission-information PDF carries 'Latest update: 28.07.2026' and the express caveat 'Subject to change'. Verified 2026-08-29. TIME-CRITICAL: the Early Bird and Late sessions for 2026/27 are closed and their ranking lists published, but the ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (18/08-04/09/2026, EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only) is OPEN at the verification date and closes at noon on 04/09/2026 — six days later — with the admission interview fixed for 11/09/2026 and no Language Centre exam session available in that window, so an applicant entering now must already hold recognised B2 proof in two languages. (1) TEACHING-LANGUAGE WEIGHTING is reconstructed from per-module language tags on the 2026/27 course-offering pages combined with the brochure study plan; the two sub-courses of 'Foundations of Psychology for Educational Work' (10 CP, tagged IT+DE) could not be resolved individually, several modules carry two language tags without a credit split, and year-3 tags are not yet published because the 2025 cohort only reaches year 3 in 2027/28. The robust conclusion — English is the smallest of the three languages and German and Italian are compulsory from semester 1 — does not depend on the exact split. (2) The study-plan HTML page reports year totals (50/51/50 CP) that do not reconcile with the brochure module list (61/60/59 CP = 180); the brochure figures are used here because they sum correctly to 180 ECTS. Foundations of General Sociology is listed as 5 CP in the brochure and 7 CP on the study-plan page. (3) SELECTION RUBRIC: the published criteria total 80 + 20 = 100 points but assign no explicit point value to the cover letter, so it is unclear whether the letter is separately scored or serves as an unscored input to the interview; no minimum passing score is published for this programme. (4) NON-EU OUTCOME: the signed Early Bird decree contains no non-EU section and the ranking-lists index publishes no separate non-EU list, indicating no non-EU applicant living abroad was admitted against the 4 reserved places — but because the Faculty of Education publishes neither scores nor exclusion lists (unlike the Faculty of Agricultural Sciences), it cannot be determined whether nobody applied or applicants were excluded. No score distribution or de facto cut-off is recoverable for this programme at all. (5) The ranking PDFs print 'Bressanone, data della firma' / 'Brixen, Datum der Unterzeichnung' rather than a typed date, so no certified signature date exists in the documents. (6) OFFICIAL NAME: the Italian name is 'Laurea in Scienze dell'Educazione' and the German 'Sozialpädagogik', per the Italian programme page and both signed decrees; automated extraction of the English page initially returned 'Laurea in Educazione Sociale' and 'Soziale Bildung', which are NOT the official names and were discarded. (7) The Italian-language admission-information PDF URL is inferred from the Italian programme title and was not directly verified. (8) PROGRAMME STATUS: 'established with a 2025 study-plan reform' is inferred from the coexistence of 'Course Offering — Enrolled from 2025' and 'Course Offering — enrolled before 2025' plus a 2025/26 brochure at the same asset path; unibz does not state a reform explicitly in English. (9) Provincial study-grant amounts (€1,680-€6,960) and the 27/30 merit threshold come from the unibz study-guide pages and are reset annually by the provincial call; they were not separately confirmed for 2026/27. There is no programme-specific scholarship. (10) No 'study career' Excel template, no bachelor-level ECTS conditional-admission threshold and no OFA apply here; the absence of OFA is affirmative (the admission document has no OFA section at all), not merely unverified. (11) Turkish-applicant relevance: Türkiye's status as a Lisbon Convention signatory (hence case (b) recognition: ARDI + CIMEA Verification) is inferred from convention membership, not stated by unibz for this programme. (12) The evidence format required to claim the 20-point social-work-experience score is not published.
